notes: POWO and FNA accept Sida abutilifolia.
Older synonyms include S. diffusa, S. filicaulis, S. procumbens, and S. supina.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with posture: this is the mat-forming Sida, with long flexible procumbent stems creeping across the ground and small pale/white-yellow flowers.
diagnostic_traits: mat-forming habit is highly distinctive in FNA

confusers.separator: S. abutilifolia sprawls/prostrates and lacks the classic erect habit with petiole-base tubercles; S. spinosa is erect and often has a small spinelike tubercle just below the petiole.

Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Malvaceae specimen index documents the taxon.
Williamson — UT Vascular Plants of Williamson County documents the taxon.
POWO confirms Texas within the native range.

morphology.key_separator: S. abutilifolia sprawls along the ground; S. spinosa is more erect and often has a small tubercle immediately below the petiole.
